newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian domestic phone charges rise 8.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian domestic phone charges rise 8.6 pct.

text.p: The Slovenian government said on Thursday it would increase charges for domestic telephone calls by 8.6 percent from Monday, while cutting rates on international calls by 18 percent.

"The price of international calls will be reduced in line with the European trend, while domestic call rates will rise in order to get closer to the European average," said Anton Grabeljsek, state secretary at the Ministry of Economic Relations and Development.
New domestic call rates will be raised to reach about 25 percent of the European average, while new international call rates would be close to their average level across Europe, he said.
Grabeljsek added Slovenia planned to increase domestic phone rates to 45 percent of the European average by the year 2000, but said further increases this year were unlikely.
